query: Starting from crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals, what single intervention could overcome the unresolved risk of structural or chemical instability during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the mechanism by which it would preserve stability, the predicted outcome relative to the same nanoparticles without the intervention, relevant temperature, time, and compositional boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a thermal-exposure experiment with measurements and failure criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a carefully designed quinary or higher refractory high-entropy alloy composition, incorporating elements that promote grain boundary stability and defect recombination, could overcome the risk of structural or chemical instability in crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime.

generation.intervention: Introduction of a carefully designed quinary or higher refractory high-entropy alloy composition
generation.conditions: Operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime
generation.mechanism: Similar principles of defect recombination and grain boundary effects as in quaternary W-Ta-V-Cr high-entropy alloy, combined with the design of a stable quinary or higher refractory high-entropy alloy composition
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved structural and chemical stability of the nanoparticles during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime
generation.baseline: Current instability issues in crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 773–1173 K and composition of five or more metals
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the exact composition and processing conditions required to achieve the desired stability, as well as potential interactions with the catalytic regime

falsification_experiment.design: In situ TEM and nanoindentation experiments on the designed quinary or higher refractory high-entropy alloy nanoparticles during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the designed nanoparticles exhibit significant structural or chemical instability during operation, the hypothesis is falsified

System: Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8 (nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25) BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
